notes.note: Navigation: begin with Theorem 1 and Question 5 in the introduction, then use the pseudo-greedy-expansion section for Corollary 10, Lemmas 12--15, Theorem 16, Proposition 19, and Corollary 20.
notes.relevance_justification: Provides the shortest source-first route through every Koizumi result cited by the public Erdos 243 paper.

notes.note: Evidence boundary: Theorem 16 proves an equivalence between Conjecture 6 and an affirmative answer to Erdős-Graham Question 5. It does not prove either open statement. Any pseudo-greedy termination claim with the same hypotheses remains a reformulation of Erdos 243, not progress past it.
notes.relevance_justification: Prevents the paper's most important citation from being misread as a solution or partial solution.

notes.note: Exact state dictionary: Lemma 15 writes x_n=c_n/d_n and epsilon_n=e_n/c_n, with e_n congruent to d_n modulo c_n in the centered interval, a_n=(d_n-e_n)/c_n+1, c_(n+1)=c_n-e_n, and d_(n+1)=d_n a_n. These are the primary-source formulas behind the public paper's (C,D,E) state system.
notes.relevance_justification: Pins every integer-state formula attributed to Koizumi rather than relying on a paraphrase.

notes.note: Exact prior-art implications: Lemma 13 proves epsilon_n=0 implies epsilon_(n+1)=0. Proposition 19(2) proves eventual epsilon_n>=0 implies eventual epsilon_n=0. Corollary 20 transports the latter back to the original reciprocal-series sequence.
notes.relevance_justification: Checks the absorption and descent priority statements made in the public paper.

notes.note: Stronger surrounding theorem: Theorem 1 reconstructs each sufficiently large a_n by nearest-integer rounding from the reciprocal-sum tail whenever |a_n^2/a_(n+1)-beta|<=1/3; if that ratio tends to beta, the rounding error tends to zero. Corollaries 2 and 3 give uniqueness characterizations of the Sylvester and Millin sequences.
notes.relevance_justification: Captures useful mathematics beyond the narrow theorem currently cited by the public paper.

None settles the unrestricted negative-gap obstruction in Problem 243.

notes.note: Published-version stronger-result locator: Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 are both on PDF p. 2 of INTEGERS 26 (2026), A28. Theorem 1 gives nearest-integer reconstruction for sufficiently large a_n under |a_n^2/a_(n+1)-beta|<=1/3, with vanishing reconstruction error when the ratio tends to beta. Corollary 1 says that reciprocal sum 1 together with 2/3<=a_n^2/a_(n+1)<=4/3 characterizes Sylvester's sequence. These are stronger rigidity results under a fixed sum and uniform ratio window, not a solution of unrestricted Erdős Problem 243. The earlier annex note n005 uses arXiv numbering; use this note for the published locator.
notes.relevance_justification: Pins the journal numbering and the exact stronger-hypotheses boundary for manuscript integration.
